text:
elaine: Drafting the Dedicated Capacity PRD for next quarter — need a quick review on SLA targets + autoscale behavior before I send to sales/legal. Main asks: 1) SLA: p99 latency target for gen endpoints 120ms, availability 99.95% for reserved pools. 2) Throughput guide: baseline pool sizing guidance (small/med/large). 3) Autoscale rules: scale-up latency threshold, cool-down, min size, burst allowances. Can folks call out immediate red flags?
sam: Quick reaction — 120ms p99 is aggressive for some open models at 8k context unless we require specific instance types or quantized variants. Do we plan to limit model catalog for SLA-backed pools?
marta: +1 on limiting catalog. Sales will want flexibility but we should map SLA to supported model families and sequence lengths. We should include a matrix: model class -> guaranteed p99 at typical seq len.
ben: For throughput, what's our unit? requests/s or tokens/s? Customers ask both. I suggest specifying both: e.g., 500 requests/s at avg 32 tokens or 2000 tokens/s. Otherwise sizing wars.
elain e: typo — meant elaine
elain e: also, edge-case: what about cold starts when scaling from 0? sales sometimes promises immediate capacity. We need an explicit warmup SLA and recommended pre-warm options.
akash: For autoscale policy proposal: scale up when p95 > 80% of target for 30s; scale down after 5m of utilization < 30%; min replicas for production pools = 2; allow burst capacity as ephemeral nodes for 90s. This gives stability but quick bursts.
liz: Can we add a fallback policy: if primary pool can't meet SLA, route to higher-cost dedicated fallback or hosted model with degraded latency SLA but no outage? That helps customer-facing SLAs.
kgomez: Legal note: SLA enforcement requires measurable SLOs + measurement window. We need to define measurement agent (edge-proxy logs) and blackout windows (maintenance, upgrades) and credits calculation. Also need error budget policy in rollout section.
elaine: Good catch. I'll add a section: "Measurement & Credits" with metrics source = edge-proxy aggregate, 1-hour rolling windows for alerts, monthly window for credits. Maintenance windows defined in contract.
sam: Load-testing plan to verify: script using k6/gatling scenario that mimics traffic shapes: steady, spike, sawtooth, cold-start ramp. Add an acceptance test that runs in CI before GA: 30m steady at 80% expected traffic, p99 < SLA.
ben: Example load command (for the PRD):
```
# k6 pseudocode
k6 run --vus 500 --duration 30m --rps 500 --http-reuse-connection --env MODEL=redwood-v1
```
Include metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, queue depth, CPU/GPU util, kv-cache hit rate.
marta: Acceptance criteria bullet list suggestion: 
- p99 < 120ms for supported model list at defined seq len
- availability >= 99.95% monthly 
- autoscale not to cause >250ms additional cold-start penalty more than 1% of requests
- failover path testable with <5s routing decision (for read routing)
- documented fallbacks and cost impact communicated to customer
These should be concrete and testable.
akash: Edge-case: burst storms that thrash autoscaler. We should add rate-limit guardrails at the ingress for reserved pools and a backpressure header so SDKs can gracefully back off.
kgomez: Add contractual language example: "Unplanned downtime excludes customer-induced errors and force majeure. Credit = (SLA - ObservedAvailability)/SLA * monthly fee capped at 50%." Legal will refine but include an example.
elaine: Can someone sanity-check the proposed pool sizes? I sketched three sku: small=1 GPU (A10g)/100 req/s, med=4 GPU/400 req/s, large=8 GPU/900 req/s. These assume quantized fp16 models and avg 32 tokens. Is that realistic?
sam: Numbers look okay but add note: model variance +/-30% depending on attn pattern and seq length. We should publish per-model adjustment factors.
ben: Also include a cost table: reserved price vs on-demand fallback. Sales needs numbers to negotiate credits and overage charges.
liz: On rollout: recommend canary: 5% traffic for 24h, 25% for 72h, then GA. Include automatic rollback on error budget burn.
akash: Operational runbook snippets:
```
# Auto-scaling knobs
- scale_up_window: 30s
- scale_down_window: 5m
- max_scale_step: 3x
- min_replicas: 2
- cooldown_after_deploy: 10m
```
Add a manual override API for on-call.
deploy-bot: Canary cluster "dedicated-prd-canary" deployed at 2025-10-08T14:12Z :rocket:
kgomez: One more: data security note for Private Dedicated customers — include KMS/HSM key usage and logging retention options. That affects SLA during migrations (keys rotation).
elaine: Thanks all. Action items I captured: 
- elaine: update PRD with model matrix, measurement section, acceptance criteria, and legal example (ETA EOD tomorrow)
- sam: draft load-test scenarios + k6 scripts by Wednesday
- akash: propose autoscale config json + runbook by Monday
- ben: pricing delta table for fallback/on-demand by Friday
- liz: rollout plan + rollback criteria doc by Thurs
- marta/kgomez: review contractual language and security section by EOW
Please react if you disagree with timelines.
sam: :thumbsup:
ben: :thumbsup:
marta: Will review, thanks
elain e: thanks everyone — I’ll ping sales after updates to align negotiation stance.
elaine: (typo again, sorry)
kgomez: Noted. Marking as blocked if legal not done before customer POC.
deploy-bot: canary traffic ramp started 2025-10-08T15:00Z (5% -> 25% over 24h)
liz: One tiny ask — include an example customer clause that clarifies "supported models" list can be updated with 30 days notice. Sales likes that.
elaine: Will add that clause. Closing thread after I push the revision.
